messages.subject: Error: Unexpected error in processing model node
parts:
Hi all,

I am building a Dirichlet process mixture regression model. However, when running buildMCMC(conf), Nimble reported the following error message:

Error: Unexpected error in processing model node: v[1, 2]Unexpected error in processing model node: pi[1, 1:10]

I have no idea what this unexpected error is. Your help would be greatly appreciated. Thank you very much!

Here's my code:
#============================
# Specify my nimble model
#============================
library(nimble)
codeModel <- nimbleCode({
  for(i in 1:N) {
    for(j in 1:J) {
      y[i, j] ~ dbern(pp[z[i], j])
    }
    z[i] ~ dcat(pi[i,1:M])
  }
  for(h in 1:M) {
    for(j in 1:J) {
      pp[m, j] ~ dbeta(shape1=1, shape2=1)
    }
  }
  for(m in 1:(M-1)) {
    knot[m] ~ dunif(0,max_x)
    invband[m] ~ dgamma(1,1)
  }
  alpha ~ dgamma(1,1)
  for(i in 1:N){
    for(m in 1:(M-1)){
      eta[i,m] ~ dbeta(1,alpha)
    }
  }
  for(i in 1:N) {
    for(m in 1:(M-1)) {
      v[i,m] <- exp(-0.5*invband[m]*(knot[m]-x[i])^2)*eta[i,m]
    }
    pi[i,1:M] <- stick_breaking(v[i,1:(M-1)])
  }
})

#============================
# Simulate my dataset
#============================
dat.sim <- function(J, K, N, props, ips) {
  trueclass <- sample(1:K, prob=props, size=N, replace=TRUE)
  dat <- matrix(0, nrow=N, ncol=J)
  for(i in 1:N) {
    dat[i,] <- rbinom(n=J, size=1, p=ips[trueclass[i],])
  }
  dat <- as.data.frame(dat)
  colnames(dat) <- paste0('Y',1:J)
  res <- list(dat = dat, trueclass = trueclass)
  return(res)
}
K <- 3
J <- 6
N <- 400
P <- c(0.5,0.3,0.2)  
pp <- matrix(c(rep(0.9,J), rep(c(0.9,0.1),c(J/2,J/2)), rep(0.1,J)), nrow=K, ncol=J, byrow=T)
set.seed(123)
simdat <- dat.sim(J, K, N, P, pp)
outcome <- simdat$dat
predictor <- rnorm(N,0,1)

#============================
# MCMC starts here
#============================
constsList <- list(N=400, J=6, M=10, max_x=max(predictor,na.rm=TRUE), x=predictor)
initsList <- list(pp=matrix(rbeta(N*J,1,1),N,J),
                  alpha=1, eta=matrix(0,N,M),
                  v=matrix(1/M,nrow=N,ncol=M),
                  pi=matrix(1/M,nrow=N,ncol=M),
                  invband=rgamma(M,1,1),
                  knot=runif(M,0,max(predictor,na.rm=TRUE)),
                  z=sample(1:8,size=N,replace=TRUE))
Data <- list(y=as.matrix(outcome))
model <- nimbleModel(code=codeModel, data=Data, inits=initsList, constants=constsList)
cmodel <- compileNimble(model)
conf <- configureMCMC(model, monitors=c('pp'), print=TRUE)
mcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)
cmcmc <- compileNimble(mcmc, project=model)
samples <- runMCMC(cmcmc, niter=10000, nburnin=2000, thin=4, setSeed=TRUE)

I actually get a different error because it looks like there is a typo in your indexing in:

```

for(h in 1:M) {
    for(j in 1:J) {
      pp[m, j] ~ dbeta(shape1=1, shape2=1)
    }
  }

```

Presumably `h` should be `m`.

I'm not sure why you are getting a different error, but perhaps that can get you started in diagnosing what is going on.
Let us know if that doesn't get you unstuck.

-Chris

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Error: Unexpected error in processing model node
parts:
Hi Cody,

It looks like we didn't anticipate this particular structure for setting up conjugate sampling for the stick-breaking case. In particular the presence of `v` in the model graph between `eta` and `pi` is revealing a bug in our conjugacy processing for the stick-breaking structure. I'll file an issue for us to fix this.

In the meantime, you can get around this by preventing use of conjugacy for sampling `eta`. Here's one way to do that:

```
conf <- configureMCMC(model, nodes = c('knot','invband','alpha','pp','z'), monitors=c('pp'), print=TRUE)  # omit `eta` from default configuration
conf$addSampler('eta', 'slice', expandTarget = TRUE)  # note: argument name of `expandTarget` is changing to `targetByNode` in nimble 1.1.0
```

I assign slice samplers to the eta values here, but you could choose something else.

    }

I'm not sure why you are getting a different error, but perhaps that can get you started in diagnosing what is going on.
Let us know if that doesn't get you unstuck.

-Chris

samples <- runMCMC(cmcmc, niter=10000, nburnin=2000, thin=4, setSeed=TRUE)
